incorrectly.  Also, fixes its use in kinematic collision
calculations.

This fixes #47029.

issue_context.title: [Godot Physics] PhysicsServer reports angular velocity with the wrong sign
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues for potential duplicates before filing yours:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue
-->

**Godot version:**
3.2.3.stable

**OS/device including version:**
N/A


**Issue description:**

If you request the angular velocity estimate of a kinematic body from the physics server with
```
PhysicsServer.body_get_direct_state(self.get_rid()).angular_velocity
```
the Godot physics value has the incorrect sign.  If you rotate with an angular velocity of `(0, 1, 0)`, then the angular velocity estimate is reported as `(0, -1, 0)`.


**Steps to reproduce:**

* Rotate a kinematic body with a fixed angular velocity: `self.rotate(Vector3(0, 1, 0), 1 * delta)`
* See that the reported `angular_velocity` value has the wrong sign: `(0, -1, 0)`

**Minimal reproduction project:**
[angular-velocity-bug.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/6142095/angular-velocity-bug.zip)
comments:
I can confirm the angular velocity seems wrong in Godot Physics and it's ok with Bullet Physics.

Here's the code in Godot Physics that calculates the angular velocity for kinematic bodies:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/6eef187a81cbdd3cd314776de372e753f79f9831/servers/physics_3d/body_3d_sw.cpp#L502-L518
I'm not sure what's wrong exactly, but the math needs to be checked. The issue is probably on this line:
`Basis rot = new_transform.basis.orthonormalized().transposed() * get_transform().basis.orthonormalized();`

Using 

```cpp
    Basis rot = new_transform.basis.orthonormalized() * get_transform().basis.orthonormalized().transposed();
```

gives the correct angular velocity.

However, it seems lots of the code is expecting "reversed" angular velocities.  For example, using `move_and_slide()` on a rotating platform:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/79001820/111310850-4202b200-86a9-11eb-9b57-e45967ebde4b.mp4

[angular_velocity_bug2.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/6149013/angular_velocity_bug2.zip)

This affects values used by rigidbodies too, so probably need to go and check everywhere that angular velocities are used.

review_comments: Better keep the `axis.normalize();` line to be safe here.

The algorithm used in `get_axis_angle()` should give a normalised axis vector, so normalising it again should be unnecessary.  To be sure, I added an assert with `Math::abs(axis.length() - axis.normalized().length()) < 1e-6` and ran my test world with many different rotating kinematic bodies, and it didn't get set off.

I'm a bit suspicious about that part of `get_axis_angle()`:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ec3f220098f4bf5a10809e6682a9a24ff93d85cb/core/math/basis.cpp#L891-L932
I have no idea if it's exact math and gives normalized axes in all cases, so I would rather be 100% safe and keep the extra `normalize()` since it's not performance critical code.
